sections.h2: Who is selling a house or unit in Fort Lee, and what do they face?
sections.html:
Fort Lee is a high-rise borough, so a quick sale usually involves the borough's Certificate of Compliance for sales, any association paperwork and, for rented units, rent leveling records. The Census Bureau lists 55.4 percent of homes as owner-occupied, which leaves close to half occupied by renters.

Fort Lee sits on the Hudson Palisades at the eastern edge of Bergen County, at the western end of the George Washington Bridge. The borough covers 2.87 square miles, 12.33 percent of it water, and counted 40,191 people in 2020. The Census estimate for July 2025 is 40,345. The 2020 density was about 15,960 people per square mile of land.

sections.h2: How did Fort Lee get here, and does the history matter to a sale?
sections.html:
Fort Lee began as a Revolutionary War outpost, then became the first center of American filmmaking, and later a skyline of residential towers. Fort Constitution was renamed Fort Lee after General Charles Lee, and in November 1776 Thomas Paine wrote The American Crisis while retreating along what is now Main Street. The New Jersey Legislature formed the borough on March 29, 1904 from remaining parts of Ridgefield Township.

Kalem began filming in Fort Lee in 1907, the Champion Film Company built the first studio in 1909, and many more studios followed during the 1910s and 1920s. The Barrymore Film Center, a theater and film museum that cost $16 million, opened in October 2022.

High-rise apartment construction along Palisade Avenue and Boulevard East began in the 1960s and raised the borough's density sharply. As of 2019 ten structures here, including the bridge, stood over 300 feet. Two 47-story towers called The Modern, finished in 2014 and 2018, are among Bergen County's tallest buildings. For a seller, this means most inventory is built after 1960 and sits under an association or a building management company.

sections.h2: What do Census figures say about Fort Lee residents and housing?
sections.html:
Fort Lee has high rents, an older population and one of the most international resident bases in the state. The table gives QuickFacts estimates for 2020 to 2024.

There are 18,287 households averaging 2.19 people, and 60.5 percent of residents age five and over speak a language other than English at home. About 43.6 percent of residents are Asian alone, and the borough is one of the largest and fastest-growing ethnic Korean enclaves outside Korea.

sections.h2: What local paperwork does Fort Lee ask of sellers?
sections.html:
Fort Lee has its own Certificate of Compliance for sales, issued through the Fire Prevention Bureau, and the borough's forms page offers a separate version for rentals. Ask the bureau for the current packet, the inspection fee and the earliest appointment before you fix a closing date.

Other borough forms a seller or landlord may need include:

  • A subcode application for a certificate through the Building Department.
  • A sidewalk permit application, if the frontage needs repair.
  • Rent leveling registration for newly rented apartments, and a separate form for a newly rented condo, co-op or one-family home.
  • A landlord identity registration form for rent leveling.
  • A tax assessor property record search and deduction forms for senior, disabled and veteran owners.

Fort Lee also has a Parking Authority that issues residential parking permits, so tell a buyer who will not have a garage how permit parking works.

sections.h2: How do condos, co-ops and associations affect a Fort Lee sale?
sections.html:
Selling a unit in a Fort Lee tower can add association steps before the deed passes. Ask the board or management office what it requires from a seller, whether it issues a resale package, and whether a buyer of a co-op unit needs board approval.

Make that request at the start of the process, before a contract is signed, so the closing date reflects the association's timetable.

For co-op units, the state classifies them as Class 4C property, and the Division of Taxation applies the graduated percent fee to them on deeds above $1 million. The fee starts at 1 percent of the total price for sales between $1,000,000 and $2,000,000 and rises in steps to 3.5 percent above $3.5 million, and the seller is responsible for it.

sections.h2: How do Fort Lee's roads and transit affect buyers?
sections.html:
Fort Lee's position at the George Washington Bridge shapes how buyers judge a property. The bridge, signed as I-95, U.S. 1-9 and U.S. 46, is the world's busiest motor vehicle bridge and carries traffic to Washington Heights in Upper Manhattan.

Roads through the borough include Route 4, Route 5, Route 67, U.S. 9W, U.S. 1/9, U.S. 46, County Route 505, the Palisades Interstate Parkway and Interstate 95. The borough had about 51 miles of roadway in 2010, and the municipality maintained roughly 35 of them.

  • NJ Transit buses 154, 156, 158 and 159 go to the Port Authority Bus Terminal in Midtown.
  • NJ Transit routes 171, 175, 178, 181, 182, 186 and 188 go to the George Washington Bridge Bus Terminal.
  • Rockland Coaches runs along Route 9W to Port Authority and the bridge terminal.
  • China Airlines and EVA Air have run private buses from Fort Lee to JFK Airport.

Mean commute time in Fort Lee is 35 minutes, nearly nine minutes above the national mean of 26.4, so buyers will ask how close a building is to a bus stop.

sections.h2: Which schools and neighborhoods define Fort Lee?
sections.html:
The Fort Lee School District serves prekindergarten through twelfth grade with six schools and had 4,074 students in 2021 to 2022. It operates four elementary schools numbered 1 to 4, Lewis F. Cole Middle School for grades 5 to 8, and Fort Lee High School. School 3 won a National Blue Ribbon award in 2010 to 2011. Students can also apply to Bergen County Technical Schools, including the Bergen County Academies in Hackensack.

The borough's named communities include Coytesville, Linwood, Palisade and Taylorville, along with the Palisade Avenue and Boulevard East tower corridor and downtown Main Street. Fort Lee Koreatown, a dining district since the mid-1980s, is a draw for visitors, and Monument Park hosts summer outdoor Shakespeare shows.

Cliffside Park, Edgewater, Englewood, Englewood Cliffs, Leonia, Palisades Park and Ridgefield border the borough. A buyer comparing prices will look at those towns too, so keep your asking price consistent with nearby recent sales.

sections.h2: What are the closing costs and filings for a Fort Lee sale?
sections.html:
The seller pays the state Realty Transfer Fee, which is based on the price recited in the deed. For a sale over $350,000, the rate is $4.80 per $500 for the band from $200,000 to $550,000, which is where a price near Fort Lee's $448,000 median value lands. The deed, the fee and the Gross Income Tax form are filed with the Bergen County Clerk.

Corporations, partnerships and multi-member LLCs file a GIT/REP-3 and check Box 5, and so do single-member LLCs. Individual sellers who live outside New Jersey owe an estimated payment of at least 2 percent of the price, or the gain times 10.75 percent if that is higher, unless the form's assurances apply. The state GIT/REP Unit answers questions at 609-322-9275.

For assessment disputes, the Bergen County Board of Taxation, 201-336-6300, handles appeals, and its page says the 2026 filing deadline has passed.

faqs.q: Does Fort Lee require a certificate to sell a home?
faqs.a: Yes, the borough issues a Certificate of Compliance for sales through its Fire Prevention Bureau. The packet is on the borough's forms page. Ask the bureau for the fee and inspection schedule before setting a closing date.

faqs.q: Are Fort Lee rentals subject to rent leveling?
faqs.a: Fort Lee has a rent leveling office with registration forms for newly rented apartments and for newly rented condo, co-op or one-family units. Landlords should confirm their registrations are current and give the buyer copies. Contact the rent leveling office for the current rules.

faqs.q: What is the mansion tax on a Fort Lee condo sale?
faqs.a: It is the graduated percent fee on deeds above $1 million, and the seller pays it. It starts at 1 percent for sales up to $2 million and reaches 3.5 percent above $3.5 million. It applies to Class 2 residential and Class 4C cooperative units.

faqs.q: How does an LLC sign the seller form in Fort Lee?
faqs.a: An LLC files the GIT/REP-3 and checks Box 5, which covers sellers that are not individuals, estates or trusts. Single-member LLCs follow the same instruction.

faqs.q: Which county office records a Fort Lee deed?
faqs.a: The Bergen County Clerk records Fort Lee deeds. The state Realty Transfer Fee and the Gross Income Tax form are filed with the deed. Your closing attorney or title company will handle the submission and confirm the fee.
